newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: APB unfazed by China losses.
newsitem.headline: APB unfazed by China losses.

text.p: Asia Pacific Breweries Ltd (APB), which is a unit of Fraser & Neave Ltd, expects more losses from its China operations, said chief executive officer Koh Poh Tiong.

"Yes, we are prepared to lose more (in China). We will have lower profits next year but we will continue to be in China. We are quite bullish about China," Koh said at briefing for analysts and reporters on the F&N group's performance.
"We will continue to make appropriate investments in China," he said.

For the year ended September 30 1996, APB lost Singapore $15.6 million from its China operations -- S$2 million was incurred by the group's joint venture company in Fujian and S$13.6 million from China Commercial Organisation, a company responsible for marketing of the group's Tiger brand.
However, on a group basis, APB's profit was flat at S$78.25 million.
Koh said he was optimistic about beer sales in China, the world's most populated country.
Beer sales in Asia Pacific is projected to grow by six percent annually against a global average of two percent, Koh said.
He said the bulk of the growth will come from China, which currently accounts for 50 percent of the region's beer consumption.
China is expected to consume 210 million hectolitres by 1999 compared to 150 million in 1995.
"Because we want to be a major player in Asia, we cannot afford not to be in China. We will continue to be in China but profitability will take time to come," Koh said.
Koh said there was keen competition from new entrants, existing players and the numerous local breweries in China. He added that he believed the brewery business there is due for a shakeout.
"The China brewery industry is at an early stage of restructuring, moving from small producers to larger ones...A day will come when international brands will come up," Koh said.
He estimated that there were now about 800 breweries in China.
